passages.text: Awake, awake, clothe yourself with strength, O Zion! Put on your garments of splendor, O Jerusalem, holy city! For the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer enter you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Zion and Jerusalem.
Zion is God's chosen people.
Jerusalem is the holy city.
God commands Zion to wake up.
God says, "Awake, awake."
God tells Zion to put on strength.
God tells Jerusalem to wear beautiful clothes.
These clothes show splendor and honor.
Jerusalem is called the holy city.
God promises a change.
God says, "No one who is uncircumcised will enter you again."
God says, "No one who is unclean will enter you again."
passages.original: עוּרִ֥י עוּרִ֛י לִבְשִׁ֥י עֻזֵּ֖ךְ צִיּ֑וֹן לִבְשִׁ֣י׀ בִּגְדֵ֣י תִפְאַרְתֵּ֗ךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ עִ֣יר הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ כִּ֣י לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֛יף יָבֹא־ בָ֥ךְ ע֖וֹד עָרֵ֥ל וְטָמֵֽא׃

passages.text: Shake off your dust! Rise up and sit on your throne, O Jerusalem. Remove the chains from your neck, O captive Daughter of Zion.
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem is the holy city of God.
Jerusalem has suffered captivity.
Daughter of Zion means the people of Jerusalem.
You are in captivity, Daughter of Zion.
Shake the dust off yourself.
Rise up from the ground.
Sit on your throne, Jerusalem.
Remove the chains from your neck.
You are no longer a captive.
passages.original: הִתְנַעֲרִ֧י מֵעָפָ֛ר ק֥וּמִי שְּׁבִ֖י יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם הִתְפַּתְּחוּ מוֹסְרֵ֣י צַוָּארֵ֔ךְ שְׁבִיָּ֖ה בַּת־ צִיּֽוֹן׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says: “You were sold for nothing, and without money you will be redeemed.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people.
The LORD says, “You were sold for nothing.
No one paid a price for you.
I will redeem you without money.
You will be set free without payment.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה חִנָּ֖ם נִמְכַּרְתֶּ֑ם וְלֹ֥א בְכֶ֖סֶף תִּגָּאֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: For this is what the Lord GOD says: “At first My people went down to Egypt to live, then Assyria oppressed them without cause.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He says this.
My people went down to Egypt first.
They went there to live.
Assyria later oppressed My people.
Assyria had no reason to do this.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה מִצְרַ֛יִם יָֽרַד־ עַמִּ֥י בָרִֽאשֹׁנָ֖ה לָג֣וּר שָׁ֑ם וְאַשּׁ֖וּר בְּאֶ֥פֶס עֲשָׁקֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And now what have I here? declares the LORD. For My people have been taken without cause; those who rule them taunt, declares the LORD, and My name is blasphemed continually all day long.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD asks, “What do I have here?”
My people have been taken for nothing.
Their rulers mock them.
The LORD says this.
People insult My name all day, every day.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֤ה מִי־ לִי פֹה֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־ לֻקַּ֥ח עַמִּ֖י חִנָּ֑ם מֹשְׁלוֹ יְהֵילִ֙ילוּ֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וְתָמִ֥יד כָּל־ הַיּ֖וֹם שְׁמִ֥י מִנֹּאָֽץ׃

passages.text: Therefore My people will know My name; therefore they will know on that day that I am He who speaks. Here I am!”
passages.sermon:
God is speaking to His people.
God says His people will know His name.
On that day, His people will understand who He is.
God Himself is the one who speaks to them.
God says, “Here I am.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֛ן יֵדַ֥ע עַמִּ֖י שְׁמִ֑י לָכֵן֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כִּֽי־ אֲנִי־ ה֥וּא הַֽמְדַבֵּ֖ר הִנֵּֽנִי׃

passages.text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace, who bring good tidings, who proclaim salvation, who say to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks to the people of Israel.
He describes messengers who bring good news.
These messengers stand on the mountains.
Their feet are beautiful because they come with a message of hope.
They announce peace.
They bring good tidings.
They proclaim salvation.
They speak to Zion.
They say, “Your God reigns.”
passages.original: מַה־ נָּאו֨וּ עַל־ הֶהָרִ֜ים רַגְלֵ֣י מְבַשֵּׂ֗ר מַשְׁמִ֧יעַ שָׁל֛וֹם מְבַשֵּׂ֥ר ט֖וֹב מַשְׁמִ֣יעַ יְשׁוּעָ֑ה אֹמֵ֥ר לְצִיּ֖וֹן מָלַ֥ךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Listen! Your watchmen lift up their voices, together they shout for joy. For every eye will see when the LORD returns to Zion.
passages.sermon:
The watchmen stand guard over Zion.
They lift up their voices.
They shout together with joy.
They see with their own eyes.
They see the LORD return to Zion.
Everyone will witness this.
The LORD comes back to His people.
passages.original: ק֥וֹל צֹפַ֛יִךְ נָ֥שְׂאוּ ק֖וֹל יַחְדָּ֣ו יְרַנֵּ֑נוּ כִּ֣י עַ֤יִן בְּעַ֙יִן֙ יִרְא֔וּ בְּשׁ֥וּב יְהוָ֖ה צִיּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Break forth in joy, sing together, O ruins of Jerusalem, for the LORD has comforted His people; He has redeemed Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The ruins of Jerusalem are empty and broken places.
God’s people once lived there.
Now, God has acted.
God has comforted His people.
God has redeemed Jerusalem.
You, ruins of Jerusalem, break out in joy.
Sing together.
God has brought hope and restoration.
passages.original: פִּצְח֤וּ רַנְּנוּ֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו חָרְב֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּֽי־ נִחַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ עַמּ֔וֹ גָּאַ֖ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: The LORD has bared His holy arm in the sight of all the nations; all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD has shown His holy power.
He did this where all nations could see.
People everywhere on earth will see this.
They will see the salvation of our God.
passages.original: חָשַׂ֤ף יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ זְר֣וֹעַ קָדְשׁ֔וֹ לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְרָאוּ֙ כָּל־ אַפְסֵי־ אָ֔רֶץ אֵ֖ת יְשׁוּעַ֥ת אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ס

passages.text: Depart, depart, go out from there! Touch no unclean thing; come out from it, purify yourselves, you who carry the vessels of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
He commands them to leave that place.
He says, “Depart, depart, go out from there!”
He warns them not to touch anything unclean.
He says, “Touch no unclean thing.”
He tells them to come out from the midst of that place.
He says, “Come out from it.”
He commands them to make themselves pure.
He says, “Purify yourselves.”
He speaks especially to those who carry the vessels of the LORD.
These people serve God in a holy way.
They must be clean and set apart.
passages.original: ס֤וּרוּ ס֙וּרוּ֙ צְא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֔ם טָמֵ֖א אַל־ תִּגָּ֑עוּ צְא֣וּ מִתּוֹכָ֔הּ הִבָּ֕רוּ נֹשְׂאֵ֖י כְּלֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: For you will not leave in a hurry nor flee in haste, for the LORD goes before you, and the God of Israel is your rear guard.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD goes before you.
The God of Israel gathers you from behind.
You will not leave in a hurry.
You will not flee in haste.
passages.original: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א בְחִפָּזוֹן֙ תֵּצֵ֔אוּ וּבִמְנוּסָ֖ה לֹ֣א תֵלֵכ֑וּן כִּֽי־ הֹלֵ֤ךְ לִפְנֵיכֶם֙ יְהוָ֔ה וּמְאַסִּפְכֶ֖ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: Behold, My Servant will prosper; He will be raised and lifted up and highly exalted.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His Servant.
God’s Servant will act wisely.
God’s Servant will succeed.
God will raise His Servant up.
God will lift His Servant high.
God will exalt His Servant very greatly.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֥ה יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י יָר֧וּם וְנִשָּׂ֛א וְגָבַ֖הּ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: Just as many were appalled at Him — His appearance was disfigured beyond that of any man, and His form was marred beyond human likeness— so He will sprinkle many nations. Kings will shut their mouths because of Him. For they will see what they have not been told, and they will understand what they have not heard.
passages.sermon:
God’s Servant appeared before many people.
Many people looked at Him and were shocked.
His appearance was disfigured more than any man.
His form was marred beyond human likeness.
He will sprinkle many nations.
Kings will see Him and become silent.
Kings will close their mouths because of Him.
They will see things they were never told.
They will understand things they never heard.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁמְמ֤וּ עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ רַבִּ֔ים כֵּן־ מִשְׁחַ֥ת מֵאִ֖ישׁ מַרְאֵ֑הוּ וְתֹאֲר֖וֹ מִבְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃ כֵּ֤ן יַזֶּה֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים עָלָ֛יו יִקְפְּצ֥וּ מְלָכִ֖ים פִּיהֶ֑ם כִּ֠י אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־ סֻפַּ֤ר לָהֶם֙ רָא֔וּ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ שָׁמְע֖וּ הִתְבּוֹנָֽנוּ׃
